paragraphs: A hydrant key is deliberately not a standard tool. The pentagon nut it fits exists so that only somebody with the right wrench can open the water, and every fire service in a region carries the same one.
The model is supplied in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and is built to CheckMate specification.
At $19 it suits emergency services and utility visualisation, equipment marketing, training material, street and site scenes, film props and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The milk variant of a jelly cup is a different product held to different rules. Dairy content changes the shelf life, the storage and often the packaging material, even when the cup looks identical on a shelf.
The model is extremely light at 1,640 polygons and 1,642 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $19 it suits food and packaging visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, kitchen and interior scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

The trigger gun is the safety device on a pressure washer. Everything upstream of it is running at full pressure whenever the machine is on, and the whole design is about that pressure stopping instantly when a hand lets go.
The model is very light at 11,083 polygons and 11,165 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 3 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $19 it suits tool and equipment visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, garage and outdoor scenes, advertising, film props and game environments. On sale since 2018.

Reconnaissance satellite panels are shaped by the same constraints as any other, with one addition: the whole spacecraft is designed not to be identified from the ground, and the array geometry is part of that signature.
The model holds 28,504 polygons and 30,128 vertices, built in quads only with mixed UV layout, in black, and carries StemCell certification.
At $19 it suits space and defence visualisation, news and documentary graphics, education material, spacecraft assembly scenes, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The twisted knot on top of a khinkali is a handle, not a garnish. It is held, the dumpling is bitten and the broth drunk, and the knot itself is traditionally left on the plate as a count of how many were eaten.
The model is extremely light at 1,208 polygons and 1,174 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $19 it suits food and menu visualisation, restaurant and packaging imagery, cultural and culinary illustration, advertising, kitchen scenes and game props. On sale since 2024.

The chocolate egg with a toy inside is banned in some countries and beloved in others, over exactly the same feature. It is one of very few products whose central idea is legally contentious rather than its ingredients.
The model is extremely light at 209 polygons and 224 vertices, built in quads only with non-overlapping UVs, so it costs nothing anywhere. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $19 it suits food and packaging visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, seasonal and children's media, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

The checkout is where a shop's whole layout terminates, and its dimensions are set by the queue rather than by the till. Belt length, bagging area and the gap a trolley has to pass through are all decided before anything else.
The model is light at 26,568 polygons and 13,325 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in grey, and carries StemCell certification. A red rigged build is offered separately.
At $19 it suits retail and interior visualisation, shopfitting presentation, store scenes, advertising, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2024.

Fertiliser is sold in bulk bags because the quantities involved make sacks absurd. One bag is a field's worth, it is lifted by a tractor rather than a person, and the printing on it is the only branding a farmer will ever see.
The model holds 7,304 polygons over 58,308 vertices, built in quads only with overlapping UVs, in white, and carries StemCell certification.
At $19 it suits agricultural and logistics visualisation, packaging presentation, farm and warehouse scenes, equipment marketing, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2026.

A single leaf is the smallest unit of a landscape and the one most often faked. Scattered on ground, floating on water or blown across a road, it is the detail that makes an environment read as outdoors rather than as a set.
The model is extremely light at 472 polygons and 470 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 3 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries StemCell certification.

At $19 it suits landscape and environment visualisation, seasonal and architectural scenes, scatter and ground dressing, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2015.
A bound notebook on a desk says something no laptop can. It signals that whatever is in it was written by hand, which is why the format survived the entire digital transition without changing at all.
The model is extremely light at 932 polygons and 996 vertices, built in quads only with non-overlapping UVs, textured with maps up to 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $19 it suits office and interior visualisation, product and e-commerce imagery, advertising, desk and study scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.
A countertop hydroponic unit is mostly a lamp. The water and nutrients are trivial; the difficult part is delivering enough light in a kitchen, and that is where the whole cost of the product goes.
The model is light at 37,290 polygons and 38,119 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in black, and carries StemCell certification.
At $19 it suits kitchen and interior visualisation, product and e-commerce imagery, advertising, sustainability and lifestyle scenes, film props and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The fat block is a teaching object rather than an anatomical one. It represents a volume of adipose tissue at scale so that a patient can hold it, and its entire purpose is that a number on a chart becomes something with weight.
The model is extremely light at 3,129 polygons and 3,131 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $19 it suits medical and nutrition education, patient explanation, clinic and fitness marketing, health campaigns and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A lit mirror is a lighting product pretending to be a mirror. The bulbs around the frame exist to remove shadows from a face, which is the one thing a bathroom ceiling light is guaranteed to get wrong.
The model is very light at 10,688 polygons and 5,550 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $19 it suits interior and product visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, bedroom and bathroom scenes, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2023.

The break glass point is designed so that raising an alarm is irreversible. Somebody who presses it has committed the building to an evacuation, and the deliberate finality of breaking something is part of the psychology.
The model is very light at 8,616 polygons and 8,624 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $19 it suits building services and safety visualisation, architectural interiors, equipment marketing, training material, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2021.
